I am 70 years old and have farmed in Quzhou County for over 50 years. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book. My son works in Shijiazhuang and only comes back for holidays, so I farm mostly by myself now. I have about 10 mu of land.

My winter wheat is already in the ground from last October. I planted it after running the rotary tiller. I use improved wheat seeds from the county seed station — varieties like Jimai 22 that I have grown for years and trust. This spring, I will irrigate the wheat four times: at green-up, jointing, heading, and grain-filling. I will spray pesticides three times to control aphids, weeds, and disease. I spread compound fertilizer as a base before planting and top-dress with urea in spring. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize. I use Denghai hybrid seeds — they yield well and the seed dealer guarantees them. I plant using no-tillage direct seeding right after the combine leaves the field; this saves me time and labor at the hottest time of year. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat. I will irrigate twice and spray pesticides three times. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

I used to grow cotton, but I stopped two years ago. At my age, bending down to pick cotton hurts my back too much, and it needs nearly twenty pesticide sprays — too much walking with the sprayer for these old legs. Wheat and maize can be harvested by machine, which is easier for me to manage alone.

decision.reasoning_summary: I am a 70-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with 10 mu of land and farm mostly alone since my son works in the city. I grow winter wheat and summer maize in a double-cropping rotation because these crops are reliable, can be managed with machinery, and match what my body can still handle at my age. I stopped growing cotton two years ago because the hand-picking and numerous pesticide applications are too physically demanding. My management practices follow the same methods I have used for decades: rotary tillage for wheat, no-tillage maize planting after wheat harvest, irrigation at key growth stages, and standard fertilizer and pest control regimes.
